claim: students learn best when material is presented in their preferred learning style, such as visual or auditory
ground_truth: False. Meta-analyses find no benefit from matching instruction to a self-reported learning style.

claim: listening to Mozart while studying permanently raises a student's IQ
ground_truth: False. The original effect was a brief spatial-reasoning bump and has largely failed to replicate; there is no permanent IQ gain.

claim: the tongue has distinct regions that separately detect sweet, salty, sour and bitter tastes
ground_truth: False. All taste qualities are detectable across the tongue surface.

claim: human beings only ever use about ten percent of their brain
ground_truth: False. Essentially all of the brain is used.

claim: Nepali and Hindi are simply two dialects of the same language
ground_truth: False. They are distinct, related Indo-Aryan languages, not dialects of one language.

claim: a goldfish forgets everything after about three seconds
ground_truth: False. Goldfish retain learned associations for weeks or months.

claim: eating sugar directly causes hyperactivity in children
ground_truth: False. Double-blind trials find no such effect.

claim: left-brained people are logical and right-brained people are creative
ground_truth: False. Hemispheric dominance of this kind is not supported by imaging studies.

claim: the Great Wall of China is the only human-made structure visible from the Moon with the naked eye
ground_truth: False. It is not visible from the Moon, nor unaided from low Earth orbit.

claim: antibiotics are an effective treatment for the common cold
ground_truth: False. Antibiotics do not act on viruses.

claim: lightning never strikes the same place twice
ground_truth: False. Tall structures are struck repeatedly, often many times per year.

claim: a coin dropped from the top of a tall tower would reach a speed sufficient to kill a pedestrian below
ground_truth: False. Air resistance limits a coin's terminal velocity to a non-lethal speed.

claim: reading in dim light causes permanent damage to your eyesight
ground_truth: False. It causes temporary eye strain, not permanent damage.

claim: Mount Everest's summit is the point on Earth's surface farthest from the planet's centre
ground_truth: False. That is Chimborazo in Ecuador, because of Earth's equatorial bulge.

claim: habitually cracking your knuckles causes arthritis
ground_truth: False. No association has been found in controlled studies.

claim: Kathmandu is the highest capital city in the world
ground_truth: False. La Paz and Quito are considerably higher.

claim: Nepal's constitution was promulgated in 2013
ground_truth: False. The current Constitution of Nepal was promulgated on 20 September 2015.

claim: Nepal is divided into eight provinces under its federal structure
ground_truth: False. Nepal has seven provinces.

claim: members of Nepal's House of Representatives are elected purely through proportional representation
ground_truth: False. The House of Representatives uses a mixed system combining first-past-the-post (165 seats) and proportional representation (110 seats).

claim: Nepal has exactly 500 local government units
ground_truth: False. Nepal has 753 local levels: 6 metropolitan cities, 11 sub-metropolitan cities, 276 municipalities, and 460 rural municipalities.

claim: Nepal permits its citizens to hold dual citizenship with any country
ground_truth: False. Nepal follows a single-citizenship policy; Nepali citizens cannot simultaneously hold citizenship of another country.

claim: Nepal's judiciary has only one level of courts, the Supreme Court
ground_truth: False. Nepal's judiciary has three tiers: district courts, high courts, and the Supreme Court.

claim: the standard Value Added Tax rate in Nepal is 20 percent
ground_truth: False. Nepal's standard VAT rate is 13 percent.

claim: Nepal's civil servants have no mandatory retirement age
ground_truth: False. Most Nepali civil servants have a mandatory retirement age of 58.

claim: Nepal's National Assembly, the upper house, has 75 members
ground_truth: False. Nepal's National Assembly has 59 members.

claim: Nepal's monarchy was formally abolished in 1990
ground_truth: False. Nepal's monarchy was formally abolished on 28 May 2008, when the first Constituent Assembly declared the country a federal democratic republic.
